analysis:
Examined three changed files.

1. ProviderLoop+Testing.swift head 514-523 adds two internal test seams. One replaces the selected-model recovery load override. The other awaits the in-progress recovery attempt. They match the existing @testable seam pattern and add no network or wire surface.

2. ProviderLoop.swift head 719-730 adds state fields: selectedModelRecovery, selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride (nil in production per its comment), savedEnabledModels and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch. Head 882 initializes savedEnabledModels from config.

3. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift head 50-54 adds three items to the local DaemonState snapshot: enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecoveryReport(). These are model-selection IDs, which are operator config and already public via heartbeats. They expose no prompts, keys or authorization material, so no A-001, A-003 or A-016 exposure was identified. The state file is local operator diagnostics (TB-003).

Not visible in this batch:
- ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, which defines the recovery load path, its no-eviction semantics, how recovery interacts with addon hold (TB-012/T-059), and the weight-hash verification on reload (T-012/T-027).
- Where savedEnabledModels and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch are updated (policy refresh and the switch path).
- selectedModelRecoveryReport contents. Integration should confirm it emits no sensitive error text.
- Whether the production load path checks selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride. It is not DEBUG-gated, but only test code sets it; integration should confirm no production setter exists.

Determining whether the recovery loads bypass the advertised-set, hash or addon-hold gates requires those unseen units.
